title: Stream graft resume protocol and toolcall semantics
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: We frequently observe partial stream replays and duplicate tool/function call emissions when clients reconnect mid-response. Current SSE resume behavior repairs byte streams but lacks a deterministic mapping of functioncall boundaries across resumes, which causes downstream tool execution duplication and broken structured outputs. Goal: introduce a graft-and-stitch resume protocol that attaches lightweight graft metadata to stream fragments, plus explicit toolcall handshake semantics so reconnects can safely reconcile in-flight function/tool calls without executing them twice. Scope: protocol changes that affect server framing, client minimal state, and runtime reconciliation layers. Non-goals: changing transport (we keep SSE/HTTP), end-to-end encryption, or changing the existing functioncall wire format beyond adding minimal graft headers/ids.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a graft id header on every chunk boundary used for resume reconciliation
Clients can request resume from a graft id and receive deterministic next-segment start without re-sending previously committed toolcall events
Runtime exposes a reconciliation hook that marks toolcall events as COMMITTED or PENDING so downstream adapters can dedupe execution
No regressions in latencies for non-resume flows (<=1% p50 increase measured on canary)
Compatibility shim supports legacy clients by mapping resume token -> graft id for 30 days after rollout
tasks: Design graft metadata envelope and minimal header format (server + client) - design doc
Implement server chunker change: emit graft ids and per-chunk sequence metadata
Runtime reconcile layer: add idempotency store for toolcall events and COMMIT semantics
Client SDK change (js/python): resume API that accepts graft id and performs two-phase handshake
Add compatibility shim in proxy to translate legacy resume tokens to graft ids
Create telemetry: metrics for resume success rate, duplicate toolcall executions, and p50/p95 latencies
Integration tests: multiplexed chat + toolcall scenario with simulated reconnects
Canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic and observe for 72 hours
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Drafted design doc; included graft id header + sequence number. Noted potential ambiguity when chunks split mid-json token — proposed chunk aligner policy that prefers semantic boundaries when possible.

2026-03-12: Runtime prototype added idempotency store for toolcall events. Local e2e shows duplicate execution eliminated for single reconnect case. Found a race when two clients reconnect concurrently to same session — added small lease window idea.
2026-03-13: SDK handshake spec reviewed by DX; requested clearer success/fail codes for resume flow (RESUME_OK, RESUME_STALE, RESUME_MISMATCH). Opened PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8123
2026-03-14: Integration tests failing on multiplexed channel ordering; investigating interaction with KV cache eviction. Added ticket ENG-659110 to follow up on eviction ordering behavior.
comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-03-12): Reviewed prototype. Concern: idempotency store growth for long-lived streams. Proposal: use a sliding window and tombstone strategy plus optional client-provided dedupe token.
Priya Shah (2026-03-13): From Security: ensure graft ids are non-predictable and not leaking sensitive offsets. We should treat graft ids as opaque nonces and rotate mapping in proxies.
Marta Ruiz (2026-03-13): UX note: SDK should expose a single resume helper that returns a reconciliation report so callers can decide whether to re-run local side-effects.
Review (2026-03-14): QA: add fuzz tests for partial UTF-8 boundary splits and long-running toolcall queue replay.
qa_plan: Create deterministic simulator that replays common reconnect patterns: (1) reconnect after N tokens, (2) reconnect during functioncall emission, (3) multiplexed channels with interleaved toolcalls. Assert no duplicate tool executions and structured output JSONL remains parseable. Add fuzz harness for boundary splits and random drops.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated server + runtime rollout. 2) Canary to 5% for 48h, monitor metrics: resume_success_rate, duplicate_toolcall_count, structured_output_errors. 3) If stable, 25% for 48h. 4) Default on and keep legacy resume token mapping active for 30 days. 5) Postmortem and doc updates.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: misrouted graft ids could cause stalling for clients on older runtime; mitigation: compatibility shim will translate tokens and reject mismatched graft ids with explicit codes so client can fall back. Risk: idempotency store resource pressure — mitigation: sliding eviction, client dedupe token, and instrumentation to alert on growth.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing the functioncall wire schema; instead it layers graft ids and a commit semantics so existing integrations (Zapier, internal tools) only need small SDK patches. Consider future work to fold graft metadata into the HTTP/2 trailers for non-SSE transports.
